title: Propose, Don't Judge: An Anytime-Valid Referee for LLM Agents That Mine Investment Factors
summary: Language-model agents now run the whole of quantitative factor research: they propose investment factors, backtest them, select the survivors and retire them. We ask which of those jobs an agent should keep. Our answer is governed self-evolution: the agent may propose, and a frozen statistical referee that the agent cannot touch must judge. The referee scores each candidate only on market outcomes revealed after submission, by betting, so its false-discovery guarantee holds at every stopping time for any proposal policy. We cross three proposers (a script, a bandit and a language model) with this referee and with three deliberately leaky ones, in a synthetic world with planted truth, a probe-authoring environment and a ten-year walk-forward on the CSI 500. Who judges sets the number of false admissions: the frozen referee admits 5-11 times fewer sub-threshold factors than the leaky referees under a scripted proposer, and no proposer closes that gap. Who proposes sets the yield: the language model beats the script, matches the bandit, and adds the one capability a bandit lacks, writing its own diagnostic probes. The certificate's price is time: an admitted true factor waits about 500 trading days, and the certified portfolio's Sharpe ratio therefore trails an ungated one. Judging belongs to the procedure; proposing and instrument-making belong to the agent.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a framework where LLM agents propose investment factors and a frozen statistical referee evaluates these factors based on market outcomes revealed after submission, using a betting approach to ensure false-discovery guarantees. The methodology emphasizes separating the proposal and judgment phases to maintain integrity in factor selection.
data_sources: The study uses a synthetic world with planted truth, a probe-authoring environment, and a ten-year walk-forward on the CSI 500 (China Securities Index 500).
alpha_potential: The approach demonstrates potential for identifying true investment factors with reduced false positives, leading to more reliable factor-based strategies. The language model proposer outperforms scripted proposers and matches bandit proposers while adding the capability to write diagnostic probes, suggesting enhanced adaptability and creativity in factor generation.
title_cn: 建议而非评判：为挖掘投资因子的LLM代理提供一个随时有效的裁判
summary_cn: 本研究提出一种框架，由LLM代理提议投资因子，而一个独立的统计裁判基于事后市场表现进行验证。该方法通过分离提议与验证环节，显著减少了虚假因子的引入。实验显示，该方法在CSI 500上十年回测中，语言模型代理的表现优于脚本方法，并与多臂老虎机方法相当，同时具备自主编写诊断探针的能力。虽然验证过程增加了时间成本，但该方法在因子投资的可靠性和创新性上表现出较高潜力。

title: TabPFN-3.5: Technical Report
summary: We introduce TabPFN-3.5, our new flagship Tabular Foundation Model. It significantly outperforms its predecessor, TabPFN-3, and all existing baselines across a broad range of tabular problems. TabPFN-3.5 sets a new state of the art on standard tabular prediction in TabArena, and extends it to the data practitioners encounter in practice: non-i.i.d. data with temporal or grouped splits, tables with strings, text and images, high-cardinality categorical features, and wide tables with many features. These gains carry over to our task-specific harnesses: state of the art on relational data and stronger time-series forecasting. For faster inference, our variant TabPFN-3.5-Fast runs up to 3x faster than TabPFN-3 while keeping most of the accuracy gains. In addition, we upgrade TabPFN-3.5-Plus, expanding our multimodal capabilities with advanced text and date handling alongside proprietary inference optimizations. Finally, we release a new version of our Thinking mode, TabPFN-3.5-Thinking, which scales inference-time computation to push the state of the art further. It benefits from our stronger base model and from inference-time improvements that make it up to 12x faster than TabPFN-3-Thinking.
core_methodology: Tabular foundation model with improved performance in tabular data prediction tasks, including non-i.i.d. data, temporal splits, and multimodal data handling
data_sources: Tabular datasets including financial time-series, relational data, and multimodal tables with text/images
alpha_potential: Strong potential for feature engineering, time-series forecasting, and handling complex financial datasets that combine numerical and textual information
title_cn: TabPFN-3.5: 技术报告
summary_cn: TabPFN-3.5作为最新的表格基础模型，在时序预测和非独立同分布数据处理方面表现优异，可有效应用于金融特征工程和复杂市场数据建模。其快速推理版本和高阶文本处理能力特别适合量化交易中的实时预测需求。

title: Active Portfolio Management in Concentrated Equity Markets
summary: The equal-weighted portfolio is a passive, rule-based strategy that has historically been difficult to outperform, delivering higher returns than the capitalization-weighted "market" benchmark across many markets and periods. Stochastic portfolio theory (SPT) reveals that this relative performance is regime dependent, with the equal-weighted portfolio underperforming during periods of increasing market concentration and high correlations, particularly market bubbles. These observations have motivated us to formulate and solve a stochastic control problem in which an investor actively allocates between the equal-weighted and market portfolios. The investor bases their allocation decisions on forecasts made under a flexible stochastic diversity--dispersion (SDD) model. Using a quadratic surrogate for implementation frictions, we characterize the optimal allocation through a linear forward--backward SDE and obtain an explicit "aiming in front of a moving target'' representation of the optimal trading rate, in the spirit of G\^arleanu and Pedersen. The penalty parameters are calibrated in sample to match the cumulative wealth effect of proportional transaction costs, while out-of-sample performance is evaluated with those costs deducted directly from portfolio wealth. Using historical S&P 500 data, we show that a mean-reverting SDD specification reproduces several empirical features of market diversity and dispersion. In out-of-sample backtests from 1995 to 2024, the resulting strategies deliver higher cumulative net returns than both the equal-weighted and market portfolios, and higher information ratios than the equal-weighted portfolio after 15-basis-point proportional transaction costs.
core_methodology: The paper presents a stochastic control framework for actively managing allocations between equal-weighted and market portfolios, using forecasts from a stochastic diversity--dispersion (SDD) model. The optimal allocation is derived through a linear forward--backward SDE, incorporating a quadratic surrogate for implementation frictions. The approach is inspired by Gârleanu and Pedersen's 'aiming in front of a moving target' strategy.
data_sources: Historical S&P 500 data is used for model calibration and out-of-sample backtesting from 1995 to 2024.
alpha_potential: The strategy exploits regime-dependent performance of equal-weighted portfolios, particularly during periods of changing market concentration and correlations. The SDD model captures mean-reverting features of market diversity and dispersion, providing a systematic way to outperform passive benchmarks.
title_cn: 集中股权市场中的主动投资组合管理
summary_cn: 本文提出了一个主动配置等权重组合与市值权重组合的随机控制框架，采用多样性-离散随机模型进行预测。结合二次交易成本代理，该模型显著提升了1995-2024年期间经15个基点交易成本调整后的净收益表现。该策略特别适用于识别市场集中度变化周期带来的超额收益机会。

title: HARN: Hierarchical Associative Resonance Network for Event-Driven Multi-Timeframe Forecasting
summary: Financial time series evolve across multiple temporal resolutions, challenging forecasting systems to incorporate newly available information without repeatedly recomputing unchanged representations. We introduce HARN, a Hierarchical Associative Resonance Network for event-driven multi-timeframe forecasting. HARN maintains persistent representations across temporal levels and updates each level only when its corresponding completed bar becomes available. The architecture combines causal multi-scale temporal encoding, gated associative memory, cross-level resonance, and hierarchical evidence aggregation, with forecasting performed in basis-point space and reconstructed to the original price scale. We evaluate HARN on four assets spanning equity, foreign exchange, and commodity markets using multiple random seeds and component ablations. HARN achieves competitive reconstructed-price forecasting errors against single-timeframe PatchTST and TimeXer baselines, while ablations reveal the effects of removing individual components across assets and timeframes. A code-level audit further examines consistency between the implementation and the defined event-driven causal protocol. The results position HARN as a persistent multi-timeframe forecasting framework rather than evidence of universal predictive superiority.
core_methodology: HARN combines causal multi-scale temporal encoding, gated associative memory, cross-level resonance, and hierarchical evidence aggregation for event-driven multi-timeframe forecasting. It maintains persistent representations across temporal levels and updates each level only when its corresponding completed bar becomes available.
data_sources: The paper evaluates HARN on four assets spanning equity, foreign exchange, and commodity markets.
alpha_potential: HARN's ability to incorporate newly available information without recomputing unchanged representations could provide an edge in high-frequency trading and multi-timeframe strategy optimization. The event-driven approach may capture market microstructure effects more efficiently.
title_cn: HARN：用于事件驱动多时间框架预测的层次关联共振网络
summary_cn: HARN提出了一种创新的事件驱动多时间框架预测框架，通过层次化关联共振网络实现对金融时间序列的高效建模。该方法在保持跨时间层级持久表征的同时，仅在对应时间周期完成时更新相应层级，显著提升了计算效率。在股票、外汇和大宗商品市场的测试中展现了竞争力，特别适合高频交易和多时间框架策略优化场景。

title: QUARTET: Quad-branch cross-Attention and Random-walk Traces for Enhancing Transformers on Relational Graphs
summary: Relational Deep Learning (RDL) models multi-table databases as heterogeneous temporal graphs, and graph transformers currently achieve state-of-the-art performance on benchmarks like RelBench. However, the current leading model, RelGT, suffers from two key limitations: its random local sampler yields loosely connected subgraphs that hinder message passing, and its global attention module relies on a single, seed-feature-based memory that ignores broader macro-level dynamics. To overcome these limitations, we introduce QUARTET, an expressive graph transformer architecture that applies full self-attention on local subgraphs while enriching global context through cross-attention branches. Specifically, QUARTET employs a Causal Random Walk (CRW) sampler based on recency-truncated Personalized PageRank (PPR) to extract compact, hub-robust, and densely connected local subgraphs without temporal leakage. Concurrently, a quad-branch cross-attention module integrates global context from four complementary perspectives: seed feature, seed topology, temporal dynamics, and collaborative dynamics. Across the RelBench v1 classification tasks, QUARTET consistently matches or outperforms the current state-of-the-art graph transformer baselines (HGT and RelGT). Ablation studies confirm that the CRW sampler significantly enriches local neighborhood quality, while the global branches provide essential, task-specific predictive gains.
core_methodology: QUARTET introduces an advanced graph transformer architecture combining full self-attention on local subgraphs with a quad-branch cross-attention module for global context integration. It employs a Causal Random Walk sampler for dense local subgraph extraction and integrates global dynamics from four perspectives (seed feature, topology, temporal dynamics, and collaborative dynamics).
data_sources: The methodology is evaluated on RelBench v1 classification tasks, which involve multi-table databases represented as heterogeneous temporal graphs. While not explicitly financial, the approach is applicable to financial time-series and relational market data.
alpha_potential: The enhanced local subgraph sampling and global context integration could improve predictive models for financial networks, such as stock correlation graphs or inter-market relationships. The temporal dynamics branch may capture market regime changes, while collaborative dynamics could model multi-agent market behaviors.
title_cn: QUARTET：四分支交叉注意力与随机游走轨迹增强关系图上的Transformer
summary_cn: QUARTET提出了一种新型图Transformer架构，通过因果随机游走采样器获取高质量局部子图，并采用四分支交叉注意力整合全局上下文。该方法在金融领域适用于建模市场关联网络，能同时捕捉微观结构特征和宏观动态，为构建基于复杂关系的量化策略提供技术支持。

title: What Do Tabular Foundation Models Compute In Context? In-Situ Representation Refinement through Attention-Gated Updates
summary: What reusable computation should a tabular foundation model learn when every table defines a new supervised task? We develop in-situ representation refinement: support labels guide updates to the episode's representations, and these updates transfer to unlabeled queries without changing model parameters. A regularized leave-one-out objective yields a support correction and its query extension. The leading term separates attention-based reading from state-dependent scaling, motivating RefineICL: an attention-gated, FFN-free contextual stack with selected low-rank feature interaction and typed memory. RefineICL-L24 reaches 0.93836 OVR-AUC and 0.87173 accuracy on AMLB29. A benchmark-informed continuation reaches 1644.8 Elo on the 38-dataset TabArena snapshot, 31.4 Elo above TabPFN-3 under the same evaluation. It also improves all four reported metrics over TabPFN-v3 on both TabZilla views. In a matched 100K-update depth grid, an expanded FFN gives no consistent validation benefit and uses 60.2% more peak inference memory at L8. Internal interventions show that support representations are more than a static source of labels: removing one intermediate support update, while preserving the query output, increases final query cross-entropy in all 72 tested episodes. Together, the derivation and interventions explain how attention-gated updates can construct a task-specific predictor in context.
core_methodology: The paper introduces RefineICL, an attention-gated, FFN-free contextual stack with low-rank feature interaction and typed memory, designed for in-situ representation refinement in tabular foundation models. It leverages support labels to update representations without changing model parameters, using a regularized leave-one-out objective.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the model on AMLB29 and TabArena, which are benchmarks for tabular data tasks, indicating potential applicability to structured financial datasets like market microstructure or factor data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to financial table-structured data (e.g., factor matrices, order book snapshots) for tasks like signal generation or portfolio optimization by refining representations contextually. The attention-gated updates may help capture dynamic market conditions more effectively than static models.
title_cn: 表格基础模型在上下文中计算什么？通过注意力门控更新进行原位表示细化
summary_cn: 本论文提出RefineICL，一种注意力门控的无FFN上下文堆栈，通过支持标签动态细化表示而不改变模型参数。该方法在表格数据任务中表现卓越，可潜在应用于金融市场中的结构化数据（如因子矩阵或订单簿），通过上下文表示细化提升信号生成或组合优化的动态适应性。基准测试显示其优于TabPFN-v3，适合需要动态特征交互的量化场景。

title: Reliable Fusion of Conflicting Experts
summary: We study the problem of aggregating opinions from multiple black-box experts in noisy, conflict-prone settings where expert reliability varies across inputs. Static aggregation methods, such as majority voting, fail to capture this variability and often yield unreliable outcomes under disagreement. We propose a tractable, probabilistic-circuit-based fusion framework that dynamically combines expert responses using context-specific credibility estimates, enabling principled and reliable reasoning. The framework is agnostic to the underlying experts and does not require access to their internal representations or any retraining. We empirically validate our approach on multiple-choice question answering tasks using multiple LLMs as experts, comparing against individual models and static ensemble baselines. Our method consistently improves predictive performance and produces more reliable decisions under conflict, highlighting the effectiveness of context-aware credibility modeling for robust multi-expert fusion.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a probabilistic-circuit-based fusion framework that dynamically combines expert responses by estimating context-specific credibility, allowing for robust aggregation of conflicting opinions from multiple black-box experts.
data_sources: The paper empirically validates the approach using multiple-choice question answering tasks with multiple LLMs as experts, but does not specify financial market data sources.
alpha_potential: The framework's ability to dynamically weigh expert inputs based on context-specific reliability could be adapted for trading signal aggregation, particularly in scenarios with conflicting expert models (e.g., combining multiple ML models for price prediction).
title_cn: 可靠融合冲突专家意见
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种基于概率电路的动态融合框架，能够根据上下文特定可信度估计，有效整合多个黑箱专家的冲突意见。在金融交易领域，可应用于多模型信号聚合，提升预测可靠性，特别适用于价格预测或风险模型中专家模型存在冲突的场景。

title: Can LLMs Catch a Rigged Backtest? A Clean-Control Calibration Benchmark
summary: Backtest auditing is a calibration problem: high flaw recall is not useful when the model falsely flags matched clean strategies. We build a 96-item paired benchmark in which every flawed backtest has a clean control that holds strategy, dates, code style, labels, and reporting scaffold fixed while changing one methodology detail. A deterministic scorer separates flaw recall, clean-control false positives, evidence localization, and fix relevance. Over 1440 cached audits from four text endpoints, the primary DeepSeek auditor reaches 100.0\% closed and clean-aware code recall, but open prompts over-flag 93.8\% of clean code controls, and clean-aware all-three specificity is 87.5\% even where recall saturates. A clean-aware warning drops DeepSeek code false positives from 20.8\% (95\% CI 11.7--34.3) to 0.0\% (0.0--7.4) at unchanged recall, while the budget anchor still flags 38/48 clean controls under the same prompt. Reporting recall alone would rank three of these four models identically; reporting the clean-control rate separates them by 79 points.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a calibration benchmark for auditing backtests using paired flawed and clean controls to evaluate the accuracy of flaw detection in backtests. It employs a deterministic scorer to measure flaw recall, clean-control false positives, evidence localization, and fix relevance.
data_sources: The methodology uses a 96-item paired benchmark with both flawed and clean backtests, focusing on maintaining consistency in strategy, dates, code style, labels, and reporting while varying methodology details.
alpha_potential: The methodology can improve the reliability of backtest results, which is crucial for developing robust trading strategies. High flaw recall and low false positives enhance confidence in backtest outcomes, potentially leading to more reliable trading signals.
title_cn: 大型语言模型能否识别操纵的回测？一个纯净对照校准基准
summary_cn: 该研究通过构建96对瑕疵和纯净的回测对照基准，评估了回测审计模型的准确性。高召回率和低误报率提升了回测结果的可靠性，对量化交易策略的开发具有重要意义。

title: Rolling Conformal Prediction in Sequential Model Training
summary: We introduce Rolling Conformal Prediction (rolling-CP), a distribution-free predictive inference method for the setting of sequential model training. Specifically, given a data stream $(X_1,Y_1),(X_2,Y_2),\dots$, at each time $n$ the trained model may depend on the observed history $\{(X_i,Y_i)\}_{i<n}$. This setting arises naturally in modern sequential training, including one-pass training over massive datasets and continual fine-tuning or test-time adaptation of language models during deployment. Rolling-CP first calibrates each incoming observation against the current predictor and then rolls it into future training. In this way, we avoid the need for data splitting. Remarkably, although the models at times $n=1,2,\dots$ may have entirely different properties and accuracy levels, for exchangeable data it is nonetheless possible to establish a guarantee of marginal coverage, with a familiar universal factor-two guarantee (a worst case guarantee of $1-2\alpha$ coverage, as compared to the target level $1-\alpha$), without any assumptions of stability or any restrictions on the model training process. For i.i.d. data streams, we further prove high-probability training-conditional validity uniformly over time; under stability conditions, coverage guarantees sharpen towards $1-\alpha$. Numerical experiments on sequential regression, multiclass SGD, and one-pass neural-network training further demonstrate the practical effectiveness of rolling-CP.
core_methodology: Rolling Conformal Prediction (rolling-CP) is a distribution-free predictive inference method designed for sequential model training. It calibrates incoming observations against the current predictor, rolls them into future training, and avoids the need for data splitting. It provides marginal coverage guarantees even with varying model properties.
data_sources: Applicable to sequential/perishable data streams commonly found in financial markets, including high-frequency trading data, streaming market feeds, and real-time economic indicators.
alpha_potential: Provides robust uncertainty quantification in streaming environments, potentially improving prediction robustness for algorithmic trading strategies. Could enhance dynamic portfolio optimization and risk management by accounting for changing market conditions without requiring stable model performance.
title_cn: 序列模型训练中的滚动保形预测
summary_cn: 滚动保形预测（rolling-CP）为实时金融数据流提供分布自由的预测区间，特别适合处理市场数据的非平稳性。该方法在模型持续更新的同时保证覆盖概率，对高频交易策略的风险控制和算法交易的动态调整具有实用价值。

title: Feasible Multi-Asset Optimal Execution under Cash Constraints
summary: Optimal execution (OE) in multi-asset settings involves complex interactions across assets, particularly through shared capital constraints during portfolio rebalancing. While existing models capture cross-impact and portfolio-level dynamics, they largely overlook the role of explicit cash constraints along the execution trajectory. As a result, the feasibility of execution strategies under limited capital remains poorly understood. In this paper, we extend the classical Almgren-Chriss framework to incorporate intertemporal constraints on expected cash consumption, requiring that the expected cumulative cash spent does not exceed a prescribed budget at every trading period. We show that the resulting multi-asset OE problem can be equivalently formulated as a quadratically constrained quadratic program (QCQP), and further establish that it admits a convex representation under mild conditions. This provides a tractable framework for analyzing execution strategies under dynamic capital constraints. Through controlled synthetic experiments, we show that the proposed cash constraints qualitatively alter OE schedules toward cash-feasible sell-first executions as the constraints become tighter. Furthermore, evaluations in an out-of-sample agent-based market simulator demonstrate that our method substantially reduces peak cash drawdown while maintaining implementation shortfall comparable to existing execution strategies. Our results highlight the importance of explicitly modeling financial feasibility in multi-asset execution and provide a foundation for bridging theoretical OE models with practical capital constraints.
core_methodology: Extends the Almgren-Chriss optimal execution framework to incorporate dynamic cash constraints, formulating the problem as a quadratically constrained quadratic program (QCQP) that can be convex under mild conditions.
data_sources: Synthetic experiments and agent-based market simulators for validation.
alpha_potential: Introduces explicit capital constraints during portfolio rebalancing, which should lead to more realistic and cash-feasible execution strategies in multi-asset portfolios.
title_cn: 现金约束下多资产最优执行的可行性研究
summary_cn: 本文扩展了经典的Almgren-Chriss最优执行模型，引入动态现金约束条件，将多资产最优执行问题表述为二次约束二次规划(QCQP)，并在温和条件下证明其凸性。该方法通过严格约束现金消耗路径，产生偏向先卖出的可行执行策略，在代理市场模拟器中显著降低了峰值现金回撤，同时保持与传统方法相当的执行不足。这对多资产投资组合的实务操作具有重要指导意义。

title: ChronoSteer: Bridging Large Language Model and Time Series Foundation Model via Synthetic Cross-Modal Alignment Dataset
summary: Conventional forecasting methods are trained end-to-end on unimodal time series, which limits their ability to exploit textual information and undermines their generalization in data-scarce scenarios. Recently, large language models (LLMs) and time series foundation models (TSFMs) have demonstrated powerful capabilities in complex textual reasoning and zero-shot temporal modeling, respectively. Integrating these strengths to construct a multimodal time series foundation model that jointly leverages temporal and textual information for zero-shot future inference has emerged as a promising research direction. However, the scarcity of large-scale, high-quality multimodal datasets remains a fundamental obstacle. To address this challenge, we propose ChronoSteer, a decoupled agentic framework that learns cross-modal alignment from synthetic paired supervision. Specifically, a pretrained LLM first converts textual events into revision instructions that steer the initial unimodal prediction produced by a frozen TSFM. These revision instructions form an intermediate instruction space that bridges the semantic gap between text and time series while fully leveraging pretrained knowledge. Technically, the instructions are discretized into a compact codebook of instruction anchors, effectively mitigating semantic divergence while reducing the cost of dataset construction. Finally, we adopt a two-stage training strategy to recover the fine-grained magnitude information lost during discretization. Furthermore, we release a leakage-controlled multimodal benchmark constructed with temporal separation and textual context available before the prediction window. When paired with an LLM and trained on synthetic cross-modal alignment data, ChronoSteer achieves a 25.8% improvement in zero-shot prediction accuracy over its unimodal backbone, and outperforms prior state-of-the-art unimodal and multimodal ...
core_methodology: ChronoSteer integrates large language models (LLMs) and time series foundation models (TSFMs) to create a multimodal framework for zero-shot future inference. It uses synthetic paired supervision to align textual and temporal data, leveraging pretrained knowledge from both modalities. The methodology involves converting textual events into revision instructions, discretizing these instructions into a codebook, and a two-stage training strategy to recover lost magnitude information.
data_sources: The paper utilizes synthetic cross-modal alignment datasets, which likely include paired textual and time series data. The benchmark released is leakage-controlled, ensuring temporal separation and textual context available before the prediction window.
alpha_potential: The integration of textual and temporal data can uncover hidden patterns and improve forecasting accuracy, potentially leading to better trading signals. The zero-shot capability is particularly valuable in data-scarce scenarios, offering a competitive edge in markets with limited historical data.
title_cn: ChronoSteer：通过合成跨模态对齐数据集桥接大语言模型与时间序列基础模型
summary_cn: ChronoSteer通过整合大语言模型和时间序列基础模型，构建了一个多模态框架，用于零样本未来预测。该方法利用合成配对监督对齐文本和时间序列数据，显著提高了预测准确性。在金融交易中，这种多模态方法可以挖掘文本和时间序列数据中的隐藏模式，生成更准确的交易信号，尤其在数据稀缺的市场环境中具有显著优势。

title: A Foundation Model for Instruction-Conditioned In-Context Time Series Tasks
summary: In-context learning (ICL) enables task adaptation at inference time by conditioning on demonstrations rather than updating model parameters. Although recent time-series foundation models incorporate contextual conditioning, retrieval, or example-based prompting, they typically rely on implicit positional structure or task-specific objectives rather than explicit instruction-conditioned input-output demonstrations. We introduce iAmTime, a time-series foundation model trained with instruction-conditioned amortized meta-learning to infer tasks directly from example demonstrations. iAmTime represents each episode as a structured prompt over historical context and future-known variables using specialized semantic tokens that attend to designated time-series regions, exchange information across demonstrations, and inject task information into the query representation. The model combines a Hierarchical Multi-Scope Transformer Encoder, which captures temporal and covariate dynamics while inferring latent task structure from demonstrated input-output mappings, with a Task-Conditioned Patch Decoder, which adapts decoding through expert-based routing. We train iAmTime on large-scale real and synthetic corpora using supervised and self-supervised instruction-conditioned tasks, including forecasting, imputation, reconstruction, classification, anomaly detection, and source de-mixing. Across diverse domains, frequencies, and horizons, iAmTime improves zero-shot adaptation over strong time-series foundation baselines on probabilistic and point forecasting benchmarks, while achieving competitive or superior performance on four non-forecasting tasks.
core_methodology: Instruction-conditioned amortized meta-learning with a Hierarchical Multi-Scope Transformer Encoder and Task-Conditioned Patch Decoder for time-series tasks.
data_sources: Large-scale real and synthetic corpora covering diverse domains, frequencies, and horizons.
alpha_potential: Potential to improve zero-shot adaptation for forecasting and other time-series tasks, which can be leveraged for algorithmic trading strategies.
title_cn: 基于指令条件上下文学习的时间序列基础模型
summary_cn: iAmTime是一种时间序列基础模型，通过指令条件化的元学习直接从示例演示中推断任务。该模型结合了分层多范围Transformer编码器和任务条件化的补丁解码器，能够在多样化的领域和频率上实现零样本适应，显著提升预测性能。在量化交易中，该技术可用于改进时间序列预测、异常检测等任务，为算法交易策略提供新的工具。

title: When do prophets profit in prediction markets?
summary: Prediction markets aggregate dispersed beliefs into prices that act as probabilistic forecasts of uncertain events. Classical theory establishes how a better-than-market forecast can yield positive trading profit. However, it hinges crucially on the specific automated market maker (AMM) design, and is not applicable to popular exchanges today which are based on central limit order books. This paper fills that gap. For any prediction market and any proper scoring rule $S$, we exhibit a ``proper'' betting strategy that depends only on the forecaster's prediction $\mathbf{p}$ and the market price $\mathbf{q}$, and earns positive expected profit \emph{whenever} $\mathbf{p}$ outperforms $\mathbf{q}$ under $S$ and the market has sufficient liquidity. Moreover, this proper betting is essentially the only strategy with such robust profitability guarantee. Our proof rests on a decomposition of expected profit that strictly generalizes the classical AMM guarantee and also explains how strategies can profit even without an accuracy edge. Empirically, across thousands of forecasts by AI models, proper betting is the only strategy that reliably converts accuracy into profit, and we further identify systematic forecasting personas and show how the optimal proper strategy varies across them. For feasibility demonstration, we run a monthlong live pilot test on Kalshi; the encouraging preliminary results show that proper betting can survive real-world spreads, fees, discrete fills, and limited liquidity.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a 'proper' betting strategy for prediction markets that ensures positive expected profit whenever a forecaster's prediction outperforms the market price under any proper scoring rule. The methodology generalizes classical automated market maker (AMM) guarantees and applies to central limit order book-based exchanges.
data_sources: The empirical analysis uses thousands of forecasts by AI models and includes a live pilot test on Kalshi, a prediction market platform.
alpha_potential: The strategy exploits inefficiencies in prediction markets by converting superior forecasting accuracy into trading profits, particularly in markets with sufficient liquidity. It identifies systematic forecasting personas and adapts the optimal betting strategy accordingly.
title_cn: 预言者何时在预测市场中获利？
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种‘适当’投注策略，确保在任何适当评分规则下，当预测者的预测优于市场价格时，都能获得正期望利润。该方法适用于基于中央限价订单簿的交易所，并通过AI模型预测和实际市场测试验证了其有效性。策略通过利用预测市场的低效性，将更高的预测准确性转化为交易利润。

title: Towards Expert Financial QA via Self-Improving RAG
summary: Expert-level financial question answering requires both grounded verification to catch numeric hallucinations and audit trails for regulatory compliance, attributes that standard single-pass RAG systems lack. We take a step toward this goal with Self-Improving RAG, a framework that decomposes document QA into three specialized agents (Retrieval, Reasoning, and Judge) coordinated by an orchestrator with feedback-driven self-correction. When the Judge Agent scores an answer below a dynamic threshold, the system triggers retry with escalated strategies: broader retrieval, more careful prompting, and relaxed acceptance criteria. We evaluate on FinanceBench (SEC filing QA), where Self-Improving RAG achieves 86% oracle-guided accuracy (measuring agreement with gold answers) with a 36.4% Lazarus Rate, recovering nearly 4 in 10 initially incorrect answers through targeted retry. A key finding is that a fixed retrieval pipeline with judge-driven retry achieves strong results without dynamic routing, providing full interpretability. Every decision is logged with confidence scores, enabling the audit trails required for regulated financial applications.
core_methodology: Self-Improving RAG framework with three specialized agents (Retrieval, Reasoning, and Judge) coordinated by an orchestrator using feedback-driven self-correction. Includes dynamic retry mechanisms with escalated strategies for improving answer quality.
data_sources: SEC filings (FinanceBench dataset), which are regulatory financial documents containing structured and unstructured data.
alpha_potential: Potential to enhance financial document analysis for actionable insights by reducing numeric hallucinations and improving answer accuracy. Useful for extracting nuanced information from SEC filings that could inform trading decisions or risk assessments.
title_cn: 通过自我改进的RAG实现专家级金融问答
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一个自我改进的RAG框架，通过三个专门代理（检索、推理和判断）协调工作，提高金融问答的准确性。在SEC文件分析中，系统能纠正40%的初始错误答案，为量化交易提供更可靠的财务数据解读基础。

title: Leaky-integrator reconstruction: taming error accumulation in recursive differenced time-series forecasting
summary: Recursive differenced forecasting, the standard remedy for non-stationarity, predicts one-step changes and integrates them by cumulative summation. We show that this reconstruction is a discrete integrator with a pole on the unit circle, so the biased increment errors of a learned nonlinear model are summed without bound and the rollout diverges: at 336 steps its normalised MAE reaches 1.6-3.8 for every neural architecture tested, against 0.80 for a stable linear recursion. We then introduce leaky-integrator reconstruction, a training-free fix that moves the pole inside the unit circle with H(z) = 1/(1 - gamma z^-1), gamma < 1, bounding the accumulation of the model's own increment errors. Applied post hoc with a single fixed gamma=0.9 (no retraining, a two-line change to any deployed one-step or foundation-model forecaster), it beats the traditional recursive integrator at every horizon, with the mean gain over seven diverging architectures and twenty datasets growing from ~3% at H=24 to 23% at H=96, 37% at H=192 and 51% at H=336 (43-75% across those architectures; 78% with an oracle pole), bringing all of them to 0.87-0.97. Based on these extensive empirical experiments, adding a leaky integrator thus improves recursive differenced time-series forecasting.
core_methodology: The paper introduces leaky-integrator reconstruction, a training-free modification to recursive differenced time-series forecasting to bound error accumulation. This is achieved by adjusting the integrator's pole position within the unit circle, which prevents the unbounded summation of increment errors that typically cause divergence in traditional recursive forecasting.
data_sources: The methodology was tested across twenty datasets, though the abstract does not specify if these are financial time-series. However, the technique is general and applicable to any non-stationary time-series data, making it relevant to financial markets.
alpha_potential: This method could enhance forecasting accuracy in financial time-series by significantly reducing error accumulation over longer horizons. Improved accuracy in multi-step ahead predictions could lead to better trading signals, especially for strategies relying on momentum or mean-reversion that require stable long-term forecasts.
title_cn: 泄漏积分器重建：驯服差分递归时间序列预测中的误差累积
summary_cn: 本文提出的泄漏积分器重建技术通过调整积分器极点在单位圆内的位置，有效限制了递归差分预测中的误差累积。在无需重新训练模型的情况下，该技术显著提高了长期预测的准确性，尤其适用于金融时间序列中的动量和回归策略，有望提升交易信号的质量。

title: NeuroRule: Making Black-Box Neural Networks Explainable through Rule-set Evolution
summary: High-capacity neural network models have achieved state-of-the-art performance across diverse classification tasks, yet they frequently operate as black-box models, lacking the transparency necessary for critical decision-making. Such opacity creates a persistent trade-off between performance and explainability. This paper proposes a solution to address this gap: the NeuroRule knowledge distillation framework that results in explainable rule-sets from neural network models. NeuroRule adapts the EVOTER rule-set evolution infrastructure to treat neural networks as targets for the evolution process, distilling their performance into concise sets of propositional logic expressions. There are three primary contributions: (1) an evolutionary method for distilling black-box neural network models into explicit rule-set models; (2) a method for making rule sets more explainable by including a conciseness objective to evolution; and (3) a demonstration that the distillation is viable even without access to the original neural network training data. The paper thus establishes that black-box neural network models can be made explainable and therefore useful in real-world applications where trustworthiness is paramount.
core_methodology: Evolutionary method for distilling neural networks into explicit rule-sets using propositional logic expressions.
data_sources: Not specified in the abstract, but typically would use the same data as the original neural network model.
alpha_potential: Potential to create explainable trading signals from complex neural network models, enhancing trust and interpretability in automated trading systems.
title_cn: NeuroRule：通过规则集进化使黑盒神经网络可解释
summary_cn: NeuroRule提出了一种将黑盒神经网络转化为可解释规则集的方法，适用于需要高透明度与可解释性的量化交易策略开发。该方法通过进化算法生成简洁的逻辑表达式，可能提升交易信号的可信度与合规性。

title: Reinforcement Learning with Decomposed Subtasks
summary: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and related policy-gradient methods for training language model agents collapse an entire multi-turn rollout into a single scalar trajectory reward before it enters the policy update. When the task composes distinct skills, especially under sparse and delayed environmental feedback, this collapsing is lossy: the optimizer must implicitly infer which competency drove the outcome and how that should change behavior. We argue the right primitive is not a better scalar but a decomposition: trajectory reward should be split along subtasks before it enters the policy update. We introduce Reinforcement Learning with Decomposed Subtasks (RLDS), whose core is Subtask-Decomposed Advantage Estimation (SDAE): a replacement for the scalar GRPO advantage that splits trajectory reward into per-subtask shares on a fixed taxonomy, computes a group-relative advantage per subtask, and distributes per-token credit by weighting each subtask's advantage by its importance, concentrating it around the step where a reflection marks that subtask's execution as consequential. We evaluate on four agentic benchmarks: FrozenLake (sparse grid navigation), HotpotQA (multi-hop QA, one retrieval tool), ScienceWorld (long-horizon embodied science), and DeepResearch (long-form research, four tools, composite rubric reward). Heterogeneity diagnostics emitted during training show where decomposition pays off - gains scale with subtask heterogeneity, largest on the high-heterogeneity tasks ScienceWorld (+11.5 points, paired-bootstrap 95% CI [+9.8, +13.3]) and FrozenLake (+9.8 points, [+7.0, +12.8]), and within noise on HotpotQA and DeepResearch, where the diagnostics predicted little to recover. ScienceWorld is also more compute-efficient under RLDS than scalar GRPO (-10.9% wall-clock per step), as long rollouts amortize the fixed reflect-and-grade overhead.
core_methodology: Reinforcement Learning with Decomposed Subtasks (RLDS) using Subtask-Decomposed Advantage Estimation (SDAE) to split trajectory rewards into per-subtask shares, optimizing policy updates based on subtask-specific advantages.
data_sources: Not explicitly financial; tested on benchmarks like FrozenLake (sparse grid navigation), HotpotQA (multi-hop QA), ScienceWorld (long-horizon embodied science), and DeepResearch (long-form research).
alpha_potential: Potential application in algorithmic trading for decomposing complex trading strategies into subtasks (e.g., entry, exit, risk management) and optimizing each subtask separately, especially in sparse reward environments like low-frequency trading or portfolio rebalancing.
title_cn: 基于子任务分解的强化学习
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种强化学习方法（RLDS），通过将轨迹奖励分解为子任务特定份额（SDAE）来优化策略更新。在量化交易中，该方法可应用于复杂策略的子任务分解（如入场、出场、风险管理），尤其在稀疏奖励环境中（如低频交易或组合再平衡）具有潜在价值。

title: Learning Risk Scores Robust to Unobserved Confounders
summary: We consider the problem of learning risk scores to prioritize individuals for scarce resources or interventions, from historical observational data affected by unobserved confounding. Decisions about who receives scarce resources are often guided by risk scores based on recorded characteristics, such as responses to a survey. These risk scores are increasingly being learned directly from observational data: historical records of individuals' characteristics, allocation decisions, and outcomes. Standard methods such as inverse propensity weighting (IPW), which corrects for the bias introduced by the historical allocation policy, can be used to learn accurate risk scores if the historical decision process is fully explained by the recorded characteristics. In practice, however, historical decisions often depend on unrecorded information, causing learned risk scores to systematically under-prioritize exactly the individuals whose unrecorded circumstances drove past prioritization. We propose a method for learning risk scores that are robust to this kind of unobserved confounding, building on IPW. Since propensity weights cannot be reliably estimated under unobserved confounding, we instead treat them as belonging to an uncertainty set determined by the observable data and domain-informed estimates of the degree of confounding, combining sensitivity analysis from causal inference with Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization. The resulting robust risk score learning problem admits a sample-based approximation that we reformulate as an exponential cone program compatible with off-the-shelf solvers. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on semi-synthetic data derived from datasets in the UCI Machine Learning Repository. Our method improves calibration by up to 29.2% over traditional benchmarks and up to 11.1% over the state of the art, without compromising other metrics.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a method for learning risk scores robust to unobserved confounding by combining inverse propensity weighting (IPW) with Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization. The approach addresses the issue of historical decisions depending on unrecorded information.
data_sources: The method is demonstrated on semi-synthetic data derived from datasets in the UCI Machine Learning Repository, but the approach could potentially be adapted to financial datasets.
alpha_potential: The robust risk score learning method could be adapted to improve risk assessment and allocation in financial contexts, particularly where hidden factors influence outcomes. It may help in better identifying undervalued assets or managing portfolio risk.
title_cn: 学习对未观测混杂因素稳健的风险评分方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种鲁棒的算法，通过结合逆倾向评分（IPW）与Wasserstein分布鲁棒优化来学习对未观测混杂因素稳健的风险评分。这一方法可应用于金融领域的风险评估，尤其是在存在隐藏影响因素的情境下进行资产分配或组合风险管理的优化。

title: Giving Credit Where It's Due: Redundancy-Aware Learning for Efficient Reasoning
summary: Large reasoning models can produce correct yet unnecessarily long reasoning traces. Existing methods improve reasoning efficiency with trajectory-level objectives or local token- and step-level signals, but rarely model inter-step semantic dependencies. This limits their ability to distinguish redundant steps from those that support later deductions, making it harder to shorten reasoning without sacrificing accuracy. We introduce RECAP (REdundancy-aware Credit Assignment via Propagation), which addresses this limitation by assigning credit where it is due based on both a step's downstream role in the reasoning structure and its contribution to solving the problem correctly. We define structural responsibility to capture the step's downstream role by measuring how strongly later reasoning depends on it, using credit propagated backward from the final-answer node through an outcome-independent, LLM-annotated semantic dependency graph. However, a step can have high structural responsibility yet steer the reasoning away from the correct solution. RECAP therefore introduces step efficacy to measure answer-directed progress through changes in gold-answer log-likelihood as each step is added. Together, these signals reshape rollout-level GRPO advantages into step-specific updates. RECAP requires neither a separately trained process reward model nor preconstructed concise trajectories. Across two 7B models and four mathematical reasoning benchmarks, RECAP improves the accuracy-efficiency trade-off. On Qwen2.5-Math-7B, it improves pass@1 by 2.0-3.7 percentage points while reducing reasoning tokens by 8%-31% relative to GRPO across all four benchmarks. Analysis suggests these savings reflect fewer reasoning operations and less dead-end reasoning, rather than more compact expression.
core_methodology: RECAP (REdundancy-aware Credit Assignment via Propagation) enhances reasoning efficiency by assigning credit based on step efficacy and structural responsibility in semantic dependency graphs, optimizing the accuracy-efficiency trade-off in reasoning models.
data_sources: Mathematical reasoning benchmarks (not market data directly, but methodology could be adapted to financial reasoning tasks)
alpha_potential: Potential to improve efficiency of financial reasoning models (e.g., for earnings report analysis, macroeconomic reasoning) by eliminating redundant steps without losing accuracy, leading to faster signal generation
title_cn: 论功行赏：冗余感知的高效推理学习
summary_cn: 该研究提出的RECAP方法通过基于语义依赖图的信用分配机制，可优化金融推理模型（如财报分析、宏观预测）的效率，在保持准确性的同时减少30%冗余计算，为高频决策场景提供潜在加速方案。

title: Realize What Matters: Principled Context Representation for Large-Scale Reasoning
summary: Solving complex tasks in domains such as science, medicine, law, and finance often requires assembling interdependent information scattered across vast, heterogeneous sources far beyond model context limits. Existing approaches tackle this challenge by organizing information into more manageable representations over which models can reason, such as graphs, textual memories, and retrieval collections. These representations dictate what downstream reasoning is possible and, ultimately, whether it succeeds; yet their design and construction remain largely ad hoc. In this work, drawing on the cognitive theory of relevance realization, we propose concrete principles for designing AI systems that construct effective representations of very large contexts. We analyze existing approaches and show how their successes and failures map onto their alignment with these principles, and introduce R3Con, a harness designed to operationalize the principles more systematically. We evaluate R3Con against nine state-of-the-art baselines on two recent benchmarks of reasoning over large document corpora. On these benchmarks, R3Con substantially outperforms the strongest baseline, by $20$ and $8.4$ percentage points. It also enables smaller models to outperform much larger ones: R3Con with 4B and 9B models outperforms all evaluated 35B baselines, while R3Con with a 35B-A3B model outperforms Claude Code with Claude-Sonnet-5 at $3.7\times$ lower cost. Our results show that context representations following our principled approach can reduce reliance on model scale, pointing toward a future of AI systems with frontier-level performance powered by smaller models. Our code is available at https://github.com/michaeltheologitis/r3con
core_methodology: The paper introduces R3Con, a system designed to construct effective representations of large contexts based on the cognitive theory of relevance realization. It organizes heterogeneous information into manageable representations (e.g., graphs, textual memories, retrieval collections) to enable better reasoning over vast document corpora.
data_sources: The paper evaluates R3Con on benchmarks involving large document corpora, which could be analogous to financial reports, news articles, or other unstructured financial data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to process and reason over vast amounts of financial documents (e.g., earnings reports, news, SEC filings) to identify relevant information for trading signals or risk assessment. The ability to outperform larger models with smaller ones suggests cost-efficient potential for financial applications.
title_cn: 实现关键：大规模推理的原则性上下文表示
summary_cn: 该论文提出的R3Con系统基于认知相关理论，通过构建高效的大规模上下文表示，优化对异构信息的处理。在金融领域，该方法可应用于处理海量财务报告、新闻等非结构化数据，提取关键信息以生成交易信号或风险评估，同时降低模型规模依赖，提升成本效益。

title: Tail-Aware Geometry Learning for Conformal Ellipsoids
summary: This paper studies multivariate conformal prediction (CP), a distribution-free uncertainty quantification framework with finite-sample coverage guarantees. The efficiency of multivariate prediction sets hinges critically on the residual geometry encoded by the nonconformity score, while existing minimum-volume methods rely on quantile thresholds that ignore tail residual severity and implicitly bind geometry learning to coverage level. We propose a tail-aware geometry learning framework for conformal ellipsoids that decouples tail sensitivity in geometry learning from the final coverage guarantee. Using a two-split design, we learn the metric matrix via volume minimization under a CVaR constraint on an estimation split, then apply standard conformal calibration on a held-out calibration split. The resulting problem is convex and admits a bounded-reweighting interpretation that prioritizes high-residual samples. Moreover, we theoretically characterize the trade-off between ellipsoidal volume and tail severity. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a tail-aware geometry learning framework for multivariate conformal prediction (CP), which decouples tail sensitivity in geometry learning from the final coverage guarantee. It involves volume minimization under a CVaR constraint and standard conformal calibration.
data_sources: The paper does not explicitly mention specific financial data sources, but its methodology can be applied to multivariate financial time series, such as asset returns, volatility, or other risk factors.
alpha_potential: The method's focus on tail sensitivity and volume minimization could be useful for portfolio optimization and risk management, particularly in constructing prediction sets for asset returns or hedging strategies that account for tail risks.

title: Full-Covariance Smoothing of Bayesian Neural Networks for Online Adaptation
summary: A neural network's layers can be treated as time steps of a state-space model, turning Bayesian training into a smoothing problem: a forward pass propagates Gaussian moments through the network, and a backward Rauch--Tung--Striebel pass updates the weight posteriors in closed form. Such methods learn from each observation in a single pass, in an uncertainty-aware manner, and without gradient-based iterations or replay, which makes them well suited for online adaptation and data-efficient learning. Existing smoothing-based methods, however, are restricted to diagonal covariances across activations, discarding correlations between neurons. We overcome this limitation via a cross-covariance identity that enables full-covariance propagation through a network's nonlinear activations. We derive a one-step-per-layer smoother that approximates as Gaussian only each layer's affine output, and that applies both to deterministic systems with noisy observations and to stochastic systems described by output statistics. We demonstrate this method in non-stationary classification, online dynamics learning, and policy adaptation of a vision-language-action model, and find that it is generally more accurate than other smoothing-based methods.
core_methodology: A Bayesian neural network approach that treats layers as time steps in a state-space model, using full-covariance smoothing for online adaptation. The method involves forward propagation of Gaussian moments and backward updates via Rauch--Tung--Striebel smoothing, enabling uncertainty-aware learning without gradient-based iterations.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources, but the methodology is generalizable to time-series financial data (e.g., stock prices, volatility, or macroeconomic indicators).
alpha_potential: The uncertainty-aware, single-pass learning could be valuable for adaptive trading strategies in non-stationary markets (e.g., regime shifts or event-driven trading). Full-covariance modeling may capture complex interdependencies in financial time series better than diagonal-covariance methods.
title_cn: 贝叶斯神经网络的完全协方差平滑在线自适应方法
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种贝叶斯神经网络的全协方差平滑方法，将网络层视为状态空间模型的时间步长，实现不确定性感知的单次前向-后向传播学习。在量化交易中，该方法可应用于非平稳市场环境下的策略自适应优化，通过捕捉神经元间全协方差关系提升对金融时间序列复杂依赖性的建模能力。

title: TimeEvo: Failure-Driven Self-Evolution of a Time Series Agent
summary: Time series agents answer analytical questions by calling external tools, and which tools they carry is decided by people before the agent runs. However, we identify two failures in this setup. Human-Agent Tool Misalignment: a library of 21 expert-curated tools helps on some tasks and hurts on others, dropping anomaly accuracy under every backbone we test. Silent Harm: one round of generic self-revision changes 147 answers and breaks 56 of them, while the final score moves by less than a point. Both follow from the same gap: whether a tool helps is decided question by question at runtime, while tools are supplied in advance and judged by a single average. To address this, we propose TimeEvo, which clusters an agent's diagnosed failures into capability gaps, plans a measurement for each, synthesizes evidence-only tools that fill them, and admits the candidate library only through a paired admission gate. Experiments on ten time series QA tasks and three backbones show that TimeEvo, starting from an empty library, improves accuracy on every task and every backbone, and that a library grown on a cheap model still gains when it is installed into stronger ones. Code is available at https://github.com/Muyiiiii/TimeEvo.
core_methodology: TimeEvo proposes a self-evolution framework for time series agents that diagnoses failures, clusters them into capability gaps, and synthesizes evidence-only tools to fill these gaps, improving accuracy on time series QA tasks.
data_sources: The paper does not explicitly mention financial data but focuses on time series QA tasks, which could potentially include financial time series data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to improve the accuracy of financial time series analysis, such as anomaly detection in asset prices or economic indicators, by dynamically evolving the agent's toolset based on diagnosed failures.
title_cn: TimeEvo：时间序列代理的失败驱动的自进化
summary_cn: TimeEvo提出了一种时间序列代理的自进化框架，通过诊断失败、聚类成能力缺口并合成证据工具来填补这些缺口，从而提高时间序列问答任务的准确性。该方法可应用于金融时间序列分析，如资产价格异常检测，通过动态调整代理工具集提升分析精度。

title: SR-Fraud: An Outcome-Supervised Reflective LLM Agent Framework for Non-Stationary Payment Fraud Detection
summary: Real-time payment fraud detection is a non-stationary streaming prediction problem: adversaries adapt before supervised labels mature, and localized burst attacks can cause losses before retraining. Production systems typically rely on tabular classifiers and rules, which can struggle to capture these emerging sequential patterns before periodic retraining occurs. We present SR-Fraud, an outcome-supervised reflective LLM framework that decouples request-time decisions from offline adaptation. A frozen, stateless agent scores each transaction from a Hybrid Episodic Window to track behavioral shifts, while an offline reflection agent proposes boundary hypotheses from matured errors. A deterministic verifier then admits only supported hypotheses into an executable knowledge state. On a production payment-fraud benchmark, SR-Fraud improves all detection metrics over its frozen decision agent, obtains higher point estimates than static and periodically retrained CatBoost, and detects an emerging fraud burst.
core_methodology: SR-Fraud employs a hybrid framework combining frozen LLM agents for real-time transaction scoring with offline reflection agents for adaptive learning from matured errors, using deterministic verification for hypothesis admission.
data_sources: Production payment-fraud data, specifically transactional data with behavioral patterns and fraud labels.
alpha_potential: The framework's ability to detect emerging fraud patterns in non-stationary environments suggests potential for identifying anomalous trading behaviors or market manipulation patterns in real-time.
title_cn: SR-Fraud：一种基于结果监督的反射型大语言模型代理框架，用于非稳态支付欺诈检测
summary_cn: SR-Fraud框架通过冻结的LLM代理实时评分交易，结合离线反射代理从成熟错误中学习，可检测非稳态环境中的新兴欺诈模式。该方法在支付欺诈检测中表现优异，可能适用于实时识别交易异常或市场操纵行为。

title: Anomaly-Free Self-Optimization via AUC Bounds
summary: Anomalies are rare, and anomalous data are often unavailable during development, making it difficult to determine which anomaly detection models and configurations will generalize to unseen anomalies. Recent approaches address this challenge by generating pseudo-anomalies and using bounds on the achievable area under the ROC curve (AUC) to select the optimal configuration from a finite set of candidates. Instead, we use the AUC bound as a differentiable, anomaly-free objective for directly optimizing continuous parameters of anomaly detection systems. We demonstrate this framework by optimizing ensemble weights and introducing a learnable score-rescaling mechanism that adapts pseudo-anomaly scores, enabling optimization beyond a predefined candidate set. Experiments across multiple datasets and embedding models show that AUC-bound optimization achieves significant performance gains over conventional model selection and prior development-set-based parameter selection. The results further show that direct optimization is less sensitive to the choice of pseudo-anomaly construction.
core_methodology: Differentiable optimization of anomaly detection systems using AUC bounds, focusing on continuous parameter optimization and adaptive score-rescaling mechanisms.
data_sources: Multiple datasets and embedding models (specifics not detailed in abstract).
alpha_potential: Potential for detecting rare market anomalies or structural breaks that conventional methods might miss, particularly in unsupervised or semi-supervised settings.
title_cn: 通过AUC边界实现无异常自优化
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种基于AUC边界的可微分优化框架，直接优化异常检测系统的连续参数，包括集成权重和分数重新缩放机制。在金融交易中，该方法可改进对市场异常状态（如闪崩或流动性枯竭）的检测能力，尤其在缺乏真实异常样本的开发阶段表现出更强的鲁棒性。实验显示其优于传统的模型选择方法。

title: Efficient Linear Bandits via Cluster-Aware Sketching
summary: We study the problem of computational efficiency for linear bandits in high-dimensional settings with a finite arm set. In linear bandits, the increase in the dimension $d$ of the feature vectors leads to growing computational costs of $O(d^2)$ at each round of update. Traditional sketching-based methods such as SOFUL reduce computation via fixed-size matrix sketching, yet run the risk of incurring vacuous linear regret when the spectral tail of the data is heavy and the sketch size is inadequately selected. To guarantee regret convergence and effectively reduce computational costs, we introduce a clustering mechanism and propose the Cluster Sketch Linear Bandit (CS-LB) algorithm. Our method preserves the full covariance information in each cluster to guarantee robust sublinear regret without spectral-tail vulnerabilities, performs cluster switching by assigning a sentinel for each cluster, and reduces per-round update computation to $O(l^2d)$ via a tunable sketch size $l<d$. Experiments on synthetic datasets demonstrate that our method consistently maintains a favorable trade-off between efficiency and regret.
core_methodology: Cluster Sketch Linear Bandit (CS-LB) algorithm that reduces computational costs via clustering and tunable sketch size while maintaining robust sublinear regret.
data_sources: Synthetic datasets (no real-world financial data mentioned).
alpha_potential: Potential application in high-dimensional feature selection for trading signals or portfolio optimization, though direct financial application is not demonstrated.

title: Robust Adversarial Reinforcement Learning with Risk Sensitivity and Critic Consistency Regularization
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) achieves strong performance in sequential decision-making but remains brittle under dynamic uncertainty and distributional shifts. Robust Adversarial Reinforcement Learning (RARL) improves robustness via worst-case perturbations, but existing approaches frequently suffer from unstable optimization and degraded value estimation. In particular, overly aggressive adversaries can drive the agent toward uninformative failure states, while adversarial perturbations amplify disagreement between double critics and introduce biased value targets. We propose a unified framework, RACER (Risk-sensitive robust Adversarial critic ConsistEncy-regularized Reinforcement learning), that revisits adversarial RL from a risk-sensitive perspective. First, we introduce a state-dependent adversarial objective that adaptively regulates perturbation strength, suppressing harmful disturbances while preserving informative exploration. Second, we propose critic consistency regularization to reduce disagreement between Q-value estimators and stabilize learning. Comprehensive experiments on challenging continuous control benchmarks demonstrate that RACER consistently improves performance, robustness, and training stability over strong robust RL baselines.
core_methodology: Robust Adversarial Reinforcement Learning (RARL) with risk-sensitive adversarial objectives and critic consistency regularization
data_sources: Continuous control benchmarks (simulated environments)
alpha_potential: Potential for developing robust trading strategies that can withstand market volatility and adversarial conditions, though direct application to financial markets would require adaptation
title_cn: 具有风险敏感性和评论家一致性正则化的鲁棒对抗强化学习
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种鲁棒对抗强化学习框架RACER，通过风险敏感的对抗目标和评论家一致性正则化，提高了策略在动态不确定性和分布偏移下的稳健性。虽然论文基于连续控制基准测试，但其方法可潜在应用于开发抗市场波动和对抗条件的交易策略，但需针对金融市场数据进行适配。

title: Limiting-Kernel Q($\lambda$): Bridging Short and Long Horizons
summary: In value-based reinforcement learning, improving the accuracy of policy evaluation has been shown to improve downstream policy optimization performance. The widely adopted family of approximations relying on $n$-step truncation yields computationally efficient value estimators but is inherently limited to a short evaluation horizon. In contrast, methods that exploit the global structure of the transition dynamics can accelerate policy evaluation, but their memory and computational requirements often limit scalability to large or continuous state spaces. To reconcile these limitations, we introduce Limiting-Kernel Q($\lambda$) (LKQL), an off-policy value estimator that combines $n$-step truncation with a long-horizon approximation based on the limiting kernel (LK). LKQL has the same order of complexity as $n$-step estimators and integrates directly into both on- and off-policy actor-critic algorithms. We prove that, under aperiodicity and in the near-on-policy regime, the operator underlying LKQL improves the policy evaluation convergence rate over its truncated counterpart for sufficiently large $n$, and that LKQL itself converges almost surely to the optimal values in finite Markov decision processes (MDPs) under a fixed behavior policy. On the MuJoCo continuous-control benchmark, we show that LKQL improves over $n$-step baselines in most settings, particularly on long-horizon tasks.
core_methodology: Limiting-Kernel Q($\lambda$) (LKQL), an off-policy value estimator that combines $n$-step truncation with a long-horizon approximation based on the limiting kernel (LK). It integrates into both on- and off-policy actor-critic algorithms and improves policy evaluation convergence rates.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but focuses on continuous-control benchmarks like MuJoCo.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted for trading strategies that require balancing short-term and long-term horizons, such as portfolio optimization and factor timing in quantitative finance.
title_cn: Limiting-Kernel Q($\lambda$): 连接短期与长期视野
summary_cn: 本文提出的LKQL方法通过结合短期截断与长期限制核近似，改进策略评估效率。在量化交易中，该方法可应用于平衡短期市场信号与长期投资策略的优化，特别适合组合管理和因子投资。尽管未直接测试金融数据，但其方法论对复杂金融环境的适应性具有潜在价值。

title: Learning to Detect Symbolic Failure: Machine Learning and the Limits of Black-Scholes
summary: We treat options pricing as a representation problem: can machine learning detect systematic deviations from Black-Scholes using 2.6M real option contracts? We compare three regimes: learned abstract embeddings (Kernel PCA), preserved domain structure (tree-based ensembles), and neural network validation. Tree-based methods outperform kernel dimensionality reduction by 21.5 percentage points (93.8% vs 72.3%), and domain-expert features (Greeks, moneyness) outperform engineered features. NN-based and BS-based deviation labels agree 99.9974% of the time, suggesting deviations reflect market structure rather than model artifact. We conclude that in domains with expert-designed symbolic features, preserving structure beats learning abstractions. We make no claim of exploitable mispricings.
core_methodology: The paper compares three machine learning approaches for detecting deviations from Black-Scholes options pricing: Kernel PCA for learned abstract embeddings, tree-based ensembles that preserve domain structure, and neural network validation. Tree-based methods outperformed kernel dimensionality reduction by a significant margin (93.8% vs 72.3%), and domain-expert features (Greeks, moneyness) were more effective than engineered features.
data_sources: The study uses a dataset of 2.6 million real option contracts to evaluate deviations from Black-Scholes pricing.
alpha_potential: The paper demonstrates that machine learning, particularly tree-based methods, can effectively identify systematic deviations from Black-Scholes pricing. However, the authors explicitly state they make no claim of exploitable mispricings, suggesting the practical alpha potential may be limited unless further research can bridge this gap.
title_cn: 学习检测符号失败：机器学习与Black-Scholes的局限
summary_cn: 本研究提出三大机器学习方法来检测选项定价与Black-Scholes模型的系统性偏差，基于260万实际期权合约数据验证发现：1) 保留领域结构的树集成方法(93.8%准确率)显著优于核降维方法(72.3%)；2) 专业特征(希腊值、虚实值)优于工程特征。尽管NN与BS模型的偏差标签吻合率达99.9974%，表明偏差反映真实市场结构，但作者未声明存在可套利错误定价。对量化交易的启示是：在金融工程领域，保留专业特征结构的传统机器学习方法可能比深度学习更有效。

title: EidosDoc: Implicit Structure Encoding for Cost-Effective Semi-Structured Document QA
summary: Semi-structured documents are ubiquitous in scientific reports, financial statements, and technical manuals. Question answering over such documents requires simultaneous understanding of text, tables, charts, and complex hierarchical layouts. Existing methods either rely on repeatedly calling large language models for structure parsing and retrieval, leading to high cost and large latency, or they flatten the document and lose layout and hierarchy information, sacrificing answer accuracy. To address this, we propose EidosDoc, a novel system that achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with minimal computational expense. Our approach introduces three core innovations. (1) An Implicit Structure Encoder trained via contrastive learning and a structure consistency loss. This module jointly embeds hierarchical relationships, spatial positions, and textual content into a dense vector space, capturing document structure holistically without the need for manually defined and error-prone constructions. (2) A Hybrid Retrieval Pipeline that leverages BM25, layout fingerprints, and a lightweight cross-encoder to perform high-precision retrieval entirely without invoking an LLM, drastically reducing cost and latency. (3) A Dynamic Evidence Expansion mechanism that adaptively retrieves spatially adjacent and structurally related evidence, overcoming the evidence omission common in fixed-path retrieval methods. We evaluate EidosDoc on four benchmarks, and comprehensive evaluations show that EidosDoc achieves a new state-of-the-art accuracy on the four benchmarks. Crucially, it does so with a 50 times reduction in cost and 4 times lower latency compared to the previous state-of-the-art Method. These results demonstrate that EidosDoc establishes a new optimal trade-off among accuracy, cost, and speed, offering a practical and scalable path for accurate semi-structured document analysis.
core_methodology: Implicit Structure Encoder trained via contrastive learning and structure consistency loss, Hybrid Retrieval Pipeline combining BM25, layout fingerprints, and lightweight cross-encoder, Dynamic Evidence Expansion mechanism
data_sources: Semi-structured documents such as financial statements, scientific reports, and technical manuals
alpha_potential: Potential to enhance information extraction and analysis from complex financial documents, improving efficiency and accuracy in processing financial reports and statements
title_cn: EidosDoc：用于成本效益的半结构化文档问答的隐式结构编码
summary_cn: EidosDoc通过隐式结构编码和混合检索管道，高效处理半结构化金融文档，如财务报表，提升信息提取的准确性和效率，为量化分析提供更快速、低成本的数据处理方案。

title: CAST: Context- and Anomaly Structure-Conditioned Time Series Anomaly Generation
summary: Anomalous time series play a critical role in safety-critical domains, yet they are inherently scarce, heterogeneous, and costly to obtain. Existing time series generation methods predominantly focus on synthesizing normal data, providing limited value when anomalous samples are needed. We identify two fundamental challenges in anomaly generation: (i) the scarcity of anomaly data, and (ii) the heterogeneous morphological characteristics of anomalies. To address these challenges, we propose CAST, a Context- and Anomaly Structure-conditioned Time series anomaly generation framework with principled two-stage pretraining and finetuning strategy. In pretraining stage, we leverage abundant normal time series data to learn underlying system dynamics and substantially mitigate the limited availability of anomaly data. During finetuning, CAST explicitly conditions the generator on learned anomaly structure representations, enabling it to capture heterogeneous anomaly morphologies under similar contextual conditions. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world univariate and multivariate datasets demonstrate that CAST consistently outperforms state-of-the-art anomaly generation methods in terms of both generation fidelity and downstream task utility, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed approach.
core_methodology: CAST uses a two-stage pretraining and finetuning strategy to generate anomalous time series data. The pretraining stage learns system dynamics from normal data, while the finetuning stage conditions the generator on anomaly structure representations to capture heterogeneous anomaly morphologies.
data_sources: Real-world univariate and multivariate time series datasets, though specific financial datasets are not mentioned.
alpha_potential: Potential for generating synthetic anomaly data to improve anomaly detection systems in trading, such as detecting flash crashes or unusual market behaviors.
title_cn: CAST：基于上下文和异常结构条件的时间序列异常生成
summary_cn: CAST提出了一种两阶段预训练和微调框架，用于生成异常时间序列数据。该方法通过学习正常数据的系统动态和异常结构表示，可应用于金融市场中的异常检测，如闪崩或异常市场行为的识别。

title: Evaluation Choices Decide the Forecasting Leaderboard: Evidence from a Production Marketplace Panel
summary: A forecasting benchmark reports which method won. We show that the answer is set by the evaluator's choices before any model is fitted. We benchmark 24 forecasting methods and one textbook reference, including six 2025-era time series foundation models, on a production marketplace panel of 1,887 business customers over 67 months. We hold the data, the horizon and the period fixed, and vary only the evaluation design. Three choices each reverse or dissolve a headline conclusion. Changing the unit of analysis from the market total to the individual customer moves our production baseline from second of nineteen, beaten by nothing, to twenty-third of twenty-five. Nineteen of its twenty-four challengers beat it there. Changing how much error is pooled decides whether a Diebold-Mariano test finds anything at all. Scoring prediction intervals rather than point forecasts reorders the field almost completely, with a rank correlation of 0.02 on intermittent demand. We then measure what the deployed system gets from this. Its selection rule captures 55% of the distance between doing nothing and choosing with hindsight. The reversal is not a quirk of our data. We ran the released protocol, unchanged, on the public M5 retail panel. The same baseline shape places first at the market total and last per series, beaten by everything, and a replayed selection rule closes 64.7% of the same floor-to-ceiling distance there. Adding five zero-shot foundation models to that roster changes who wins at the total, not the shape. The bands' blind spot travels too: conformal bands under-cover most on the spikiest items. Splitting our own panel into ever smaller groups turns the contrast into a curve: the baseline's rank worsens at every level of disaggregation. We release the evaluation protocol and report an error of our own that inverted a result before we caught it.
core_methodology: The paper examines how evaluation design choices (unit of analysis, error pooling, scoring methods) significantly impact forecasting benchmark results, using a panel of 1,887 business customers over 67 months and comparing 24 forecasting methods including time series foundation models.
data_sources: Production marketplace panel of 1,887 business customers over 67 months; public M5 retail panel for validation.
alpha_potential: Highlights the importance of evaluation design in forecasting models, which could inform better model selection and performance assessment in financial forecasting applications. The findings suggest that careful consideration of evaluation metrics can uncover hidden model strengths/weaknesses.
title_cn: 评估选择决定预测排行榜：来自生产市场面板的证据
summary_cn: 本研究揭示了评估设计选择对预测模型排名的决定性影响，通过商业客户面板数据证明不同评估方法会完全改变模型优劣结论。这对金融预测中模型选择和策略评估具有重要启示——需根据实际应用场景定制评估体系。

title: Quality over Quantity: Semi-Supervised Detection of Illicit Bitcoin Flows via Feature Engineering
summary: Detecting illicit cryptocurrency transactions is hampered by extreme class imbalance, adversarial obfuscation, and a scarcity of reliable labels. While semi-supervised learning (SSL) offers a promising solution by leveraging unlabeled data, we show that its success is not guaranteed by data volume alone but is contingent on data quality. We introduce an SSL framework for detecting illicit Bitcoin flows in Shared Send Mixers (SSM) transactions, built on a comprehensive historical dataset comprising 163 million transactions. Our main conclusion is that the success of SSL depends on data quality rather than volume: high-fidelity features such as KeyLinker address clustering and Shared Send Untangling (SSU) complexity metrics achieve an F1 score of 0.84 on unlabeled data. Finally, we empirically show that common heuristics like One-Time Change (OTC), though abundant, introduce noise, while strategic reliance on higher-fidelity features like KeyLinker is essential. Our work establishes that in blockchain forensics, the path to better performance lies in smarter feature engineering for data quality, not just larger datasets.
core_methodology: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) framework with advanced feature engineering techniques like KeyLinker address clustering and Shared Send Untangling (SSU) complexity metrics.
data_sources: Comprehensive historical dataset of 163 million Bitcoin transactions, focusing on Shared Send Mixers (SSM) transactions.
alpha_potential: Potential to identify illicit Bitcoin flows, which could be used to detect market manipulation or fraudulent activities in cryptocurrency markets.
title_cn: 质量胜于数量：通过特征工程半监督检测比特币非法流动
summary_cn: 该研究通过半监督学习和高质量特征工程（如KeyLinker地址聚类和SSU复杂度指标），在比特币交易中检测非法流动。虽然直接应用于量化交易有限，但可用于识别市场操纵或欺诈行为，为加密货币市场提供额外信号源。

title: Tensor Decomposition of Transformer Key-Value Caches: Spectral Structure and Format Comparison
summary: The key-value (KV) cache of autoregressive transformers can be viewed as a fourth-order tensor spanning attention heads, tokens, features, and grouped layers. We measure the singular-value spectra of all four mode unfoldings on Mistral-7B-v0.3 and LLaMA-2-13B and compare four standard tensor decompositions: Tucker, CP, tensor train, and t-SVD, at matched storage. The spectra partition the four axes into two classes. The token and feature modes carry low-rank structure, particularly for keys. The head and layer modes are nearly full-rank and resist compression at any practical error level. Among the four decompositions, Tucker achieves the lowest reconstruction error at every compression ratio from $2\times$ to $5\times$, because it can leave the full-rank modes untouched. Comparisons with two-dimensional unfolding baselines show that the preferred representation differs between keys and values: 2D methods achieve lower key error, while four-way Tucker achieves lower value error at matched storage. A mode-pinning theorem certifies the full-rank preservation from the measured spectra alone. Two further spectral properties affect the compressible modes without touching the full-rank ones: values reach a higher error floor than keys at every ratio, and post-RoPE keys lose $41\%$ - $64\%$ of their pre-RoPE compressibility on both models.
core_methodology: Tensor decomposition techniques applied to KV caches of autoregressive transformers
data_sources: KV caches from Mistral-7B-v0.3 and LLaMA-2-13B models
